prompt: Company profile: Snack-food manufacturer in Columbus, Ohio; 120 employees; single plant running two shifts. Situation: The company is installing a new automated packaging line (case erector, powered conveyors, robotic palletizer). Maintenance technicians will clear jams and perform servicing that requires reaching into the equipment, and the line has electrical, pneumatic, and stored mechanical (spring/gravity) energy sources. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
# Compliance Obligations Register: Automated Packaging Line Installation  
**Company:** Snack-food manufacturer, Columbus, Ohio (120 employees, single plant, two shifts)  
**Equipment:** Case erector, powered conveyors, robotic palletizer (electrical, pneumatic, stored mechanical energy)

---

## **A. Occupational Health & Safety (ISO 45001) Obligations**

### **1. Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Program**
- **Requirement:** Develop machine-specific energy control procedures; provide training for authorized, affected, and other employees; conduct annual inspections of each procedure; supply locks/tags/hardware.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.147 (OSHA)  
- **Applicability:** Directly applies to servicing equipment with multiple energy sources (electrical, pneumatic, spring/gravity). Each piece of equipment (case erector, conveyors, robotic palletizer) requires distinct procedures.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Annual audit of all LOTO procedures; quarterly supervisor spot-checks during maintenance; review of near-miss reports; employee interviews.  
  - **When:** Within 30 days of installation; annually thereafter; after any incident or equipment modification.

### **2. Machine Guarding & Point-of-Operation Protection**
- **Requirement:** Install guards to prevent contact with nip points, pinch points, and rotating parts; provide interlocked perimeter guarding around robotic palletizer; ensure emergency stops within arm's reach.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.212, 1910.219 (OSHA)  
- **Applicability:** Conveyors have transfer points; robotic palletizer creates struck-by/crushing hazards; case erector has moving forming mechanisms.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Pre-operational inspection by qualified person; monthly safety team audits; functional testing of interlocks and e-stops.  
  - **When:** Before commissioning; monthly during operations; after any jam or guard removal.

### **3. Robot Safety & Risk Assessment**
- **Requirement:** Conduct risk assessment per ANSI/RIA R15.06; implement safety-rated soft limits, area scanners, or light curtains; ensure control reliability and fault tolerance.
- **Source:** ANSI/RIA R15.06-2012 (industry consensus standard), OSHA General Duty Clause  
- **Applicability:** Robotic palletizer installation creates high-severity hazards; standard is "other requirement" for due diligence.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Third-party risk assessment verification; integration testing records; fault simulation drills.  
  - **When:** During factory acceptance testing; after installation before production; annually or after programming changes.

### **4. Electrical Safe Work Practices & Arc Flash**
- **Requirement:** Label electrical panels with arc flash warnings; provide PPE category ratings; train qualified persons on safe work practices; maintain approach boundaries.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.305, 1910.333; NFPA 70E (industry best practice)  
- **Applicability:** Packaging line has 480V panels, VFDs, and control circuits requiring energized troubleshooting.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Annual infrared thermography; review of energized work permits; PPE inventory checks; employee competency assessments.  
  - **When:** Before first energized work; annually; after any electrical incident.

### **5. Stored Mechanical Energy (Gravity/Spring Hazards)**
- **Requirement:** Develop specific procedures to block, bleed, or cage stored energy; install mechanical stops for vertical conveyors; verify zero-energy state before entry.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(5) (OSHA)  
- **Applicability:** Explicitly identified in scenario—case erector springs and gravity zones on conveyors/palletizer.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Job safety analysis (JSA) review; visual inspection of blocking hardware; technician demonstration of procedure.  
  - **When:** During LOTO procedure validation; quarterly field observations; after any jam-clearing incident.

### **6. Ohio Workers’ Compensation & Safety Committee**
- **Requirement:** Establish a safety committee with management and labor representatives; meet quarterly; document minutes and corrective actions; report serious injuries to BWC within 24 hours.
- **Source:** Ohio Revised Code 4123.54; Ohio BWC Policy  
- **Applicability:** Ohio employer with 120 employees in manufacturing (hazardous industry threshold >50 employees).
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Review committee minutes and attendance; verify injury reporting logs; BWC audit participation.  
  - **When:** Quarterly (per meeting schedule); annually during BWC policy renewal; after any lost-time injury.

---

## **B. Environmental (ISO 14001) Obligations**

### **7. Solid Waste Management & Recycling**
- **Requirement:** Properly store and dispose of packaging waste (cardboard, plastic film, broken pallets); maintain manifests for off-site recycling; prevent stormwater contamination.
- **Source:** Ohio EPA (ORC Chapter 3734); RCRA (40 CFR 262)  
- **Applicability:** Manufacturing process generates significant packaging waste; facility is in Columbus (Franklin County EPA jurisdiction).
- **ISO 14001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Monthly waste stream audits; quarterly vendor manifest reviews; dumpster inspections for contamination.  
  - **When:** Monthly; quarterly; annually during Ohio EPA compliance review.

### **8. Energy Performance & Resource Consumption**
- **Requirement:** Monitor electricity and compressed air consumption from new line; set improvement targets; consider energy efficiency in procurement.
- **Source:** Ohio Revised Code 4923.01 (energy policy); voluntary ISO 50001 alignment  
- **Applicability:** New automated equipment increases energy demand; ISO 14001 requires resource planning.
- **ISO 14001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Other requirements—energy policy)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Track kWh and CFM usage via submeters; compare baseline vs. actual consumption; review in management review.  
  - **When:** Monthly for first 6 months post-installation; quarterly thereafter; annually in management review.

---

## **C. Cross-Cutting Obligations**

### **9. Pre-Startup Safety Review (PSSR)**
- **Requirement:** Complete PSSR checklist verifying all safety systems (guards, LOTO, E-stops, interlocks) are installed and functional before first production run.
- **Source:** OSHA PSM 1910.119(j) (applicable by analogy); internal policy  
- **Applicability:** New equipment installation with high-hazard energy sources; best practice for operational readiness.
- **ISO 45001/14001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Documented sign-off by maintenance, safety, and operations managers; punch-list completion verification.  
  - **When:** Prior to commissioning; after any major modification.

### **10. Contractor Management (if applicable)**
- **Requirement:** Ensure installation contractors follow site safety rules; verify their LOTO training; maintain oversight during commissioning.
- **Source:** 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(8); OSHA Multi-Employer Citation Policy  
- **Applicability:** If OEM/vendor technicians perform installation/startup.
- **ISO 45001 Clause:** 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements)  
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2):**  
  - **How:** Daily safety briefings; contractor log review; observation of contractor work practices.  
  - **When:** Throughout installation phase; at contractor demobilization.

---

**Note:** All obligations map to **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** or **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** (identification of legal/other requirements). Evaluation methods align with **9.1.2** (evaluation of compliance) requiring periodic review, measurement, and analysis of performance data.
